title: Identity coherence of scalar operation comparisons
statement: Let l be prime. Coefficient fields are finite extensions of Q_l with specified Q_l-algebra embeddings. Use the actual completed coefficient sheaves and raw rationalizations of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Schemes supporting a constructible rational category are assumed noetherian, finite-dimensional, with l invertible; ambient operation comparisons are for arbitrary scheme morphisms g : X → Y in the actual ambient derived categories. For a finite coefficient-field embedding, the direct-image and ordinary-pullback scalar comparison transformations for an identity scheme morphism respect the canonical derived operation units. The completed-pullback comparison likewise respects the fixed completed identity isomorphism, with completion units retained.

source.place: Order 1307; existing scalar-extension component, relocated without changing signatures or proofs.

proof.text: For the identity morphism, compose the identity-on-sections scalar/restriction comparison with the ordinary direct-image identity comparison. The section formula for each coefficient datum shows this equals restriction of the target direct-image identity comparison. Apply conjugateEquiv to the two composite adjunctions. Conjugation of whiskering, composition and the unitors then gives the ordinary scalar/pullback identity equation.

Evaluate on a flat-term K-flat complex P. Its scalar extension is again flat-term K-flat. Postcompose the desired derived pullback identity with the invertible scalar cochain counit. Naturality of this counit, the defining scalar comparison equation, and the two derived identity normalization equations reduce it to the ordinary identity equation from the first step, applied degreewise. Resolve an arbitrary derived object by such a complex and use naturality along the resulting isomorphism to obtain the identity on every object.

The direct-image comparison is the actual mate of the ordinary-derived pullback comparison. Expand the mate into unit, right-adjoint image of the square and counit. Naturality of the conjugate identity comparison moves it across the last two factors. The unit/conjugate equation and the pullback identity equation cancel the identity isomorphism and yield the direct-image identity equation. Specialize the two equations to the actual finite coefficient inclusion.

Keep the existing completed identity proof: precompose both routes with the completion unit. Naturality and the unit-normalized scalar completion comparison reduce them to the ordinary-derived identity equation. The reflection-unit hom extensionality property cancels the unit, since the target is complete.
